note: Live: two Work tabs open in one browser, idle for 30 s after settling, made 1 /api/ request each (one GET /api/v1/inbox). No refetch loop; the 91 requests per tab are the first-load burst.

The Cockpit now installs a beforeunload guard and a Back/Forward guard that hold the move while any editor is dirty, then open the leave review. Code read; not exercised live (needs a dirty editor and a real reload).

Programmatic focus in record lists first scrolls the row into view (scrollToIndex for windowed lists, scrollIntoView for bounded ones) and only then focuses with preventScroll, so the focused row stays visible. Code read.

A forced-colors block now keeps focus, selection, current page, tabs, menu highlight and disabled state visible (live screenshot with forced colors on). But the primary button has no border, so 'New task' reads as plain text in that mode, and the filled running dot has no border either (code only; the sandbox has no running run).

finding.title: In Windows high-contrast (forced colors) the primary button loses its outline and reads as plain text
finding.trigger: Turn on forced colors (Windows high contrast, or Playwright forcedColors) and open Work: 'New task' is the only header action with no border. With a run queued, the sidebar Work dot (filled, no border) also disappears.
finding.expected: Every button keeps a visible boundary and status marks keep a shape or border in forced colors.
finding.actual: The accessible-controls forced-colors block recolors borders for buttons, but the primary variant is bg-accent with no border, so nothing is drawn; the running dot is background-only. The screenshot shows 'New task' unframed beside three framed buttons.

note: CockpitShell still imports ChatArea statically. Live (dev server): loading /inbox requested ChatArea.tsx and 71 modules under areas/chat. Production chunk size not measured here.

finding.title: Opening any non-Chat page still loads the whole Chat module graph
finding.trigger: Open /inbox (or /system) cold and record the module requests.
finding.expected: Non-Chat first loads defer the Chat stack until Chat is opened.
finding.actual: CockpitShell statically imports ChatArea, so 71 chat modules (including ChatArea.tsx) load on /inbox and /system. Only the Chat render is deferred (retainedChat), not the code. Dev-server module counts, not production bytes. No load time was measured, so this is recorded as a structure issue, not a timing one.

note: DESIGN-DECISION: Risk badges and help text now go through one presenter and read Safe, Caution, Danger, Nuclear everywhere, which is the wording DESIGN.md lines 54, 60 and 71 specify. The old review's Low/Medium/High/Critical labels were a design alternative that was never adopted; the policy enum values are unchanged.
Approval cards are named through presentApprovalAction; live the Inbox shows 'Review shell exec' with a plain policy reason and a Danger badge, and target detail sits under 'Show source context'.

Menu and palette highlight now draw a 2px accent outline, and the focus ring is !important so no unlayered rule strips it. The accent against canvas, raised and overlay is 5.4 to 11.1:1 in both themes (computed from the tokens).

Tabs now carry an accent underline when selected (and an outline in forced colors), but the sidebar current page and the selected conversation row still use the same bg-sunken tint as hover. Live: current and hovered sidebar links share rgb(15,29,45); only the text colour differs slightly.

finding.title: The current page in the sidebar looks the same as a hovered one
finding.trigger: Open Work, hover another sidebar link and compare it with the highlighted Work row.
finding.expected: The current item differs from hover in more than a faint tint (marker, weight or an accent edge) in both themes.
finding.actual: Both use bg-sunken (1.06:1 against the dark canvas); current only switches text from fg-secondary to fg. The same pair of classes is used on conversation rows and messaging rows.

note: Every rail destination now resolves to a native owner; Classic opens only through the explicit ?shell=classic rollback. The only remaining embedded Classic pages are Prompt packs and the Ops Kanban (WorkKanban.tsx:66, LibraryPromptPacks.tsx:85), not the approval, question, failed-run, health or settings tasks the row named.

The Cockpit has its own sign-in gate, and once it has mounted a lost session only hides the shell (Activity hidden, inert) so unsaved drafts stay mounted. Code read; token-mode sign-in was not exercised (the token Gateway is not running).
Handoffs to Classic add shellScope=visit, and the shell switch skips writing the saved preference for a visit, so only the explicit 'Switch to classic Mission Control' persists.

Links to a nonexistent 'Ops' or 'Approvals' are gone because the Classic handoffs themselves are gone. Classic is still named four ways: 'Switch to classic Mission Control', 'Open the classic view', 'This view is available in Classic', 'classic Kanban'.

finding.title: Classic is still called four different things in the Cockpit
finding.trigger: Open the account menu, the palette (Ctrl+K), a Classic-only URL and the Ops Kanban run view.
finding.expected: One name for the other layout everywhere.
finding.actual: Sidebar.tsx:280 'classic Mission Control'; cockpit-compatibility.ts:187 'Open the classic view'; CockpitShell.tsx:220 'Classic'; WorkKanban.tsx:54 'classic Kanban'.

note: AreaErrorBoundary wraps the whole shell, Chat, Projects and each area; it shows a recovery panel (with a stale-build reload for failed lazy chunks) and resets on scope change. Code read; a render error was not forced live.

The Work dot carries sr-only text and a title, and running (filled, pulsing) differs from unknown (hollow ring); health uses an icon plus label; the collapsed stream state is a focusable tooltip with a name. Not checked with a screen reader.
recordView keeps the last good record while a background read runs or fails (phase 'checking', stale flag), 28 areas use it, and a repo check script guards the pattern.

Live at 375 px with touch: buttons, selects, tabs and nav links are at least 44 px. Plain text links stay 32 to 36 px (above the 24 px AA minimum, below the 44 px goal) and 'Advanced setup' is 17 px, which is under 24 px. Compact density not tested.

finding.title: On a phone, the 'Advanced setup' link on Capabilities is only 17 px tall
finding.trigger: At 375 px wide with touch, open Capabilities > Connectors and measure 'Advanced setup'.
finding.expected: Touch targets are at least the 24 px AA minimum (44 px is the product goal).
finding.actual: 'Advanced setup' is 17 px tall. Other plain links measured 32 to 36 px (above 24 px, under the 44 px goal) and are not part of this finding.

note: Live, the seven landing pages (desktop and phone) showed no raw ids, ISO times, JSON or enums, and recorded errors go through presentErrorText. Running the raw-values script's own counting (ids inside TechnicalDetails are stripped) on the Cockpit still finds the browser-session actor id printed as visible text in System > Browser sessions (code read, not reproduced live; the sandbox has no browser grant).

finding.title: System > Browser sessions prints the raw actor id as visible text in grants and grant reviews
finding.trigger: Code read, not reproduced live: System > Browser sessions, open a session's grants list, or press the review button for a new grant, a rotation or a revoke.
finding.expected: Names come first; ids appear only under technical details.
finding.actual: BrowserGrantReview.tsx:16 renders 'Actor: {request.actorId}' (also :47, :55, :59); BrowserSessionGrants.tsx:212 renders {grant.actorId} in each grant row, outside the TechnicalDetails at :227; the every-host warning at :372 reads '{review.request.actorId} can use this session'. The script's own comment treats browser-session actor ids as the grant's visible subject, so this may be intended; no other visible raw-id case was confirmed.

note: Every area page draws the h1 first, then its tab row, and the default tab (Work Board, Library first tab, System Health) matches the route; screenshots of Work, Library and System show it.

Live: selecting a Work task or run, a Library capability or tab, a System tab and a Chat conversation each put the record in the URL and Back returns to the list. In Inbox, 'Review' on an approval leaves the URL at /inbox, so the selection is local state and not a link. finding.title: The Inbox item you open is not in the URL, so Back, reload and sharing lose it

finding.expected: The selected item has a deep link, like Work tasks and runs (/work/tasks/<id>).

note: Risk badges use their own Shield and ShieldAlert icons while lifecycle status uses spinner, hand, check, cross and circle, all with text labels; the Work and System screenshots show distinct icons.

finding.title: Memory detail shows 'Owner: ws_...' as a raw id with no link

finding.expected: The responsible workspace is named, and linked when it can be opened.

note: git grep finds no result copy crediting 'the Gateway' for an operator decision; settlement text says 'Approved. …'. The two remaining 'The Gateway …' strings (mail-draft-failure.ts:58, :68) describe runtime evidence accurately.

note: An unlayered reduced-motion rule sets animation: none !important on every cockpit element, beating the older 0.01ms reset in the base layer (cockpit.css:198); the sandbox had no running animation to compare, and status stays as text.

The shell-scoped focus ring is unlayered and !important so no other rule strips it, and the tab strip (a scroll container) draws its ring inside with outline-offset -2px. DESIGN-DECISION: The surface values (canvas, raised, sunken, overlay) are exactly the hex pairs in DESIGN.md's colour table (line 30) and line 48 specifies 'Flat surfaces with hairline borders', so the flat ladder (dark canvas to sunken 1.06:1) is the documented design; separation comes from borders.

DESIGN-DECISION: The text tiers are exactly the values in DESIGN.md's colour table (line 31). The current values are the documented design and the readability floor is met: every tier is at least 5.2:1 (light) and 7.8:1 (dark) on the surfaces, above the 4.5:1 body-text rule.

Measured by characters: 12 px and 13 px text is 86.9% (Inbox), 89.9% (Capabilities), 92.0% (Settings), 94.2% (Library), 95.5% (Chat), 99.2% (System) and 99.7% (Work) of visible text; 14 px is 0% on Work. This is the DESIGN.md-scale body size, so this is a density observation, not a measured safety-copy problem.

finding.title: Almost all body and safety copy is 12 or 13 px

finding.expected: Primary and safety copy reads at 14 px or larger, with comfortable line length.
finding.actual: 12 px and 13 px make up 87 to 99.7% of characters on the landing pages (Work 99.7%, System 99.2%, Chat 95.5%, Library 94.2%, Settings 92.0%, Capabilities 89.9%, Inbox 86.9%); no safety-relevant copy was shown to fall below the design scale.

The budget still measures the one entry script named in index.html (450 KB cap). That script is the small main.tsx stub, which loads the Cockpit with import("./cockpit-entry"), so the Cockpit and Chat chunks are only checked by the 900 KB per-lazy-chunk cap.

note: cockpit.css is still a bare @import "tailwindcss" with no source() or @source, so Tailwind scans its default base (the whole app folder, including Classic, tests and mockups). The shared package uses no Tailwind classes, so no styling is missing; the cost is build work and extra CSS.

finding.title: Tailwind still scans the whole app folder (Classic, tests, mockups)

finding.expected: The scan lists the real Cockpit sources, with visual regression proof.
